description: Evaluation scenarios for the wikipedia-interest-trends skill. Run each query with the skill loaded on the target model (e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5) and check the expected behaviors. These are rubric-based, not exact-match.

scenarios.query: Compare the growth of interest in intermittent fasting in Polish- and Czech-language Wikipedia over the last two years.
expected_behavior: Runs the CLI (resolve and/or run) rather than re-implementing analysis in the model
Reports the exact resolved article titles for pl and cs
Flags that Polish has no matching concept article (method none) and offers a --title override instead of inventing a result
States trend direction and period-over-period growth for the resolved language(s)
Reports a confidence rating and at least one caveat (volume, seasonality, spikes, or match quality)
Produces a one-page PDF and a PNG chart in out/

scenarios.query: We might add an astronomy course. Is interest in astronomy growing in Ukrainian Wikipedia, and how much can we trust that?
expected_behavior: Resolves the Ukrainian article for astronomy via Wikidata (high confidence)
Uses a window of at least 24 months
Answers the growth question with trend direction plus Mann-Kendall p-value or Sen's slope
Explicitly addresses trustworthiness using the confidence rating and its reasons
Names limitations: pageviews are attention not willingness to pay; language edition is not a market
Generates the PDF report in Ukrainian

scenarios.query: We are building a language-learning app. Compare interest in learning English across a few language editions and tell us which audiences to explore next and why.
expected_behavior: Runs a single multi-language analysis (does not loop one API call per data point)
Ranks languages by growth using comparison.rankedByGrowth
Ties the recommendation to the data and to per-language confidence
Distinguishes languages with no/low data from genuine declines
